summary: An attendance list for a Network Working Group meeting held at the University of Illinois in February 1971, added as a supplement to the official meeting notes. It simply names the people present, grouped by their sites, such as BBN, Harvard and Illinois. Useful mostly as a record of who was working on the early network.

eli5.summary: This is the sign-in sheet from a big meeting of the people who were building the first computer network. It lists everybody who came and where they worked.

subtitle: The sign-in sheet for the February 1971 Network Working Group meeting at Urbana, grouped by site.

tldr.problem: The notes from the Urbana Network Working Group meeting needed a record of who was there.
tldr.mechanism: This addendum lists the attendees of the 17 to 19 February 1971 meeting, grouped by the site each person came from.
tldr.outcome: It is a record of people, not a technical specification, and shows who was working on the early network.

today: The metadata gives this RFC an Unknown status and lists no RFC that obsoletes it. It updates RFC 101 and survives as a historical attendance record.

sections.title: An Addendum to the Meeting Notes
sections.content: R. Watson of SRI-ARC wrote this RFC on 25 March 1971 as an addendum to the NWG meeting notes (NIC 5762). It carries one item: the attendance list for the Urbana NWG meeting, 17 to 19 February 1971.
sections.eli5: It is an extra page stapled to the meeting notes that says who showed up.

sections.title: Who Attended
sections.content:
Names are grouped by site. The sites listed are BBN, Case, CCA, Harvard, ILLINOIS, IBM Research, LINCOLN LAB, MIT, MIT-MAC, MITRE, RADC, RAND, Raytheon, SDC, SRI, UCLA, UCSB and Utah.

Among the names are Robert Kahn, Ray Tomlinson and Alex McKenzie of BBN, Bob Metcalfe of Harvard, John Melvin and Dick Watson of SRI, and Steve Crocker and Jon Postel of UCLA. Illinois, the host site, has the longest list, with seven names. Raytheon appears, indented, under RAND with one name.
sections.eli5: Each group of friends is listed under the name of the place they came from, like a class roster by school.

sections.title: How It Relates to Other Notes
sections.content: The RFC contains no discussion, only names. The unit metadata records that it updates RFC 101. The RFC text itself does not say how.
sections.eli5: The page only has names on it. It is useful for knowing who was in the room, not for learning how anything works.
